A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AMRIV research. Their text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching renumbered and relocated material.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix F report original synthetic and TripAdvisor-based semi-synthetic simulations, including estimation error, efficiency, and confidence-interval coverage in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix H retain these original simulation results, displayed in Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: Appendix C introduces an optional self-normalized kernel variance estimator instead of the floored difference-of-moments estimator. This adds a procedural alternative, while Algorithm 1, adaptive allocation, cross-fitting, and the AMRIV estimator remain unchanged. The alternative is not evaluated experimentally.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five-dimensional synthetic environment and ten-dimensional TripAdvisor-based semi-synthetic simulator. Their data-generating processes and treatment-effect estimation tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Both experiments retain AMRIV-NA, DM, DM-NA, A2IPW, Oracle, Oracle-NA, AMRIV-MS, and DM-MS as comparators or variants. Newly discussed methods in related work and Appendix C are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Both versions report T = 2000, a 200-round burn-in, updates in batches of 200, and the same truncation schedule and random-forest configurations. Normalized MSE, MSE, and 95% interval coverage remain the evaluation metrics. Appendix C's implementation alternatives do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The adaptive versus non-adaptive comparisons and deliberate nuisance-misspecification tests are retained in both simulation settings. No additional ablation, sensitivity test, robustness experiment, or empirical stopping-time analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1000 independent trials, empirical standard errors, and the same confidence-interval reporting. The seed of 1 for the fixed synthetic coefficient vector is also retained. The new checklist reiterates existing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The empirical plots are identical after matching v1 Figures 2–3 to v2 Figures 3–4, including curves, error bars, and comparator labels. No numerical result entries or substantive empirical findings are added. The new early-stopping diagram is schematic.

T1.justification: The main assumptions and theorem statements are retained. Appendix E restores a missing plus sign between variance terms, and Appendix F.2 removes an extra subtraction of tau in the martingale expectation. Appendix C adds the kernel-estimator formula and cited nuisance convergence rates; the existing proofs are otherwise largely unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: variance-optimal adaptive instrument assignment, semiparametric efficiency, multiply robust consistency, asymptotic normality, convergence rates, and confidence sequences.

C2.justification: New Remark 1 asserts an ACLATE interpretation when unconfounded compliance fails. Section 4 expands the explanation of outcome and compliance noise, and Appendix C adds computational qualifications, including potentially quadratic kernel-update cost. The original limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix C provides learner-selection guidance and incremental, block-update, and sufficient-statistic implementation options. The checklist also discloses LLM assistance with writing and debugging. Existing experimental hyperparameters, hardware, runtime, and replication-code access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A broaden the adaptive-design discussion with works including Neopane et al. (2025), Li et al. (2024), and Lee and Ma (2024). Additional references address weak instruments and nuisance learning. The central positioning against direct-treatment designs and prior adaptive-IV methods remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction and portions of related work and results discussion are rewritten or expanded. Notation and implementation appendices, acknowledgements, and a conference checklist are added, alongside title and affiliation edits. Most exposition and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 1 illustrating the experimental workflow and early stopping, plus notation and nuisance-estimator tables. Existing figures are renumbered and repositioned without changing their plotted content. Algorithm 1 and the overall manuscript layout remain similar.

improvement.justification: The new schematic, notation table, and implementation guidance make the paper easier to understand and use, while local algebraic corrections improve precision. The empirical evidence and central guarantees are unchanged. The gains are qualified by Remark 1's ACLATE identification claim without an explicit monotonicity condition, but the presentation and documentation improvements provide a modest net benefit.
